questions.question: What quantity does the mole measure?
Approximately how many specified entities are in one mole?
What is molar mass?
choices: Mass of every sample regardless of size
Mass per mole of a substance

questions.question: Which unit commonly expresses molar mass?
What is a limiting reactant?
choices: The reactant with the greatest mass in every case
The reactant that restricts the maximum product amount
A catalyst that slows the reaction

questions.question: What is theoretical yield?
choices: The product actually isolated in every experiment
The mass of all equipment used
The maximum product predicted from the reaction stoichiometry

questions.question: What is percent yield?
choices: Theoretical yield divided by actual yield, multiplied by 100
Actual yield multiplied by molar mass
Actual yield divided by theoretical yield, multiplied by 100
Reactant mass divided by elapsed time

questions.question: Why do equal moles of different substances not generally have equal masses?
choices: The substances can have different molar masses
Each mole contains a different Avogadro number
Equal numbers of entities require equal entity masses

questions.question: Why are coefficients useful for mole conversions?
choices: They state identical masses for all substances
Their ratios relate amounts of substances in the balanced reaction

questions.question: Why must an equation be balanced before stoichiometric calculations?
choices: Unbalanced equations always predict zero product
The conversion ratios must correctly reflect atom conservation
Molar mass depends on the equation's layout

questions.question: How is a sample's amount in moles obtained from its mass?
Why can excess reactant remain after a reaction finishes?
choices: All reactants must have equal starting mass
Excess reactants do not contain atoms
A balanced equation requires leftover products
Another reactant can be used up first

questions.question: Why can an actual yield be below the theoretical yield?
choices: Incomplete reaction or product loss can reduce recovered product

questions.question: Why should the counted entity be identified when using moles?
choices: A mole can refer to atoms, molecules, ions, or other specified entities
A mole always refers only to whole organisms
Moles change size depending on the unit symbol
Every molecule contains exactly one atom

questions.question: What is a useful check on a stoichiometric calculation?
choices: Ignore the balanced equation if numbers look small
Assume grams and moles are interchangeable
Track units and compare the result with available reactant amounts
Round every input to zero decimal places

questions.question: A substance has molar mass 20 g/mol. How many moles are in 40 g?
What is the mass of 3 mol of a substance with molar mass 10 g/mol?
For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many moles of water can 4 mol H₂ produce with excess O₂?
For N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, a mixture contains 1 mol N₂ and 2 mol H₂. Which reactant limits the reaction?
choices: Neither; the mixture has the exact ratio
